design:
## Design tests

The refined visuals and the new placement rules were then read blind in six whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v018.md`), the waver, the one template the v0.17 gate failed, put in all six, so each could only stand where its hand is clear of the backdrop's lines and not at the far back. The wave read as a wave in all six, every time "with motion lines", and no reader saw a string or a held object at the raised hand. No reader saw two figures drawn into each other, a ball heading for someone other than the catcher, a duck's wake reaching anyone or a thing cut off by the picture's edge. The sleeping cat read as asleep in all four scenes it was in, and no reader there called it small; the dark-haired woman read as reading as she walks, though her "facial features are minimal".

Nothing in the test scenes led to a further change before the set was built.
intro: The waver, the one template that failed the v0.17 gate, passes the fifteenth screen: read as a wave in all four of its pictures, and no reader saw a string at the hand. The refined visuals read as meant: the dark-haired woman was in 16 pictures, ten in profile, and no reader said her face was missing; the larger cats read as asleep and as stalking on the grass; catches kept their bodies apart. But the set scored 0.986 over all items (0.995 in v0.17), with 1.9 unintended oddities per picture (1.3), and 60 of 64 templates pass the gate. Four that passed in full in v0.17 fall short, each in a single picture: the reading walker in the windy tier-4 park, read as "holding an open newspaper" and not seen as about to trip; the stalking cat on the tier-4 garden's fence, read as walking; the frying pan in a probe beside a hose reel, read as "a hose nozzle or watering wand", the first misread anywhere in four screens; and a runner read as "striding or jogging". `vision/flaws_v018.md` lists them with their fixes for v0.19.
screen: Across all 60 pictures only 10 of 720 scored items fell short of full marks (4 of 748 in v0.17), and one, in a probe, was misread: the frying pan, held nearly edge-on beside a hose reel, read as a hose nozzle. In the set nearly every shortfall came from two tier-4 pictures: in the garden a cat on the fence top read as walking and a boy's raised arms under a ball in a tree as "cheering, stretching or waving"; in the park a teenager reading as she walks, her book held wide in a windy picture, read as "holding an open newspaper", and the bucket ahead of her as having "no obvious owner or purpose". Unintended oddities rose from 27 to 40 in the set and from 35 to 41 in the probes (39 probe pictures, 44 in v0.17). None of the v0.17 oddities came back as reported then: no figures of different events drawn into each other, no face hidden by hair, no filler cut off by the edge, no duck's wake reaching anyone. What the readers noticed instead: figures drawn tight against tall things (a photographer "inside the swing frame", a woman "tightly overlapping the lamp post", a begging dog against a woman's legs); children reaching for a ball in a tree who stand "beside the trunk, not under the stuck ball"; kicks that look like a miss and painters whose painted boards are beside them; water drawn as dashes, "readable as a dotted trajectory"; and, again, goats out of place and market stalls with nobody at them.
redrawn: The waver passes at 1.00 over four pictures, its hand clear of the backdrop's lines. Catches (four pictures) and the larger sleeping cat (three) read with full marks, the cat "curled up asleep" each time, though one probe reader still found it "small"; the duck feeding missed half a point only where its reader did not say the duck wanted the bread. The stalking cat read in full on the grass and as walking on the fence, and the reading walker, read in full in three pictures, fell short in the windy tier-4 park (below).
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (50 in three, 11 in four, 1 in five, 1 in six, 1 in seven). Four fail, each in a single picture, and all four read in full in v0.17: the reading walker in the windy tier-4 park, the stalking cat on the tier-4 garden's fence, the frying pan beside a hose reel in a probe (one misread) and a runner read as "striding or jogging". About five templates of the gate's movement between screens is reader variance (the v0.9 retest), but each of these has a cause in its picture that can be fixed. The v0.19 fixes: no reading walker in a windy picture or at the far back, the stalking cat on a fence closer to its bird, no hose reel beside the pan waterer and the pan turned to show its inside, and motion lines behind a runner.
